results.name: One Arm Push Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your feet wide and one hand under your chest.
Place your other hand behind your back.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your body straight.
Press back up and repeat, then switch arms.
tips: Widen your feet for balance.
Start with your hand on a raised surface.
results.description: One Arm Push Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core, Obliques.

results.name: Pec Deck Fly Machine Flies
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles or place your forearms on the pads, arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest.
Return slowly to the open position and repeat.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Don't let the weight stack slam between reps.
results.description: Pec Deck Fly Machine Flies is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders.

results.name: Plate Deficit Pushup
instructions: Place two weight plates on the floor shoulder-width apart and put a hand on each.
Get into a push-up position.
Lower your chest below the level of your hands.
Press back up and repeat.
tips: Only go as deep as your shoulders allow.
Keep your body in a straight line.
results.description: Plate Deficit Pushup is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Plate Glute Bridge to Chest Press
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, holding a weight plate at your chest.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a bridge.
Holding the bridge, press the plate straight up over your chest.
Lower the plate, then lower your hips and repeat.
tips: Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Keep your ribs down while pressing.
results.description: Plate Glute Bridge to Chest Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps.

results.name: Plate Press
instructions: Stand or lie down holding a weight plate at your chest, squeezing it between your palms.
Press the plate straight out in front of you while squeezing your hands together.
Pause with your arms extended.
Bring the plate back to your chest and repeat.
tips: Squeeze the plate hard the whole time.
Keep your shoulders down.
results.description: Plate Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Push Pull Front Handle Push
instructions: Sit tall on the machine and take the front handles at chest height.
Brace your core with your back against the pad.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight.
Return slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't lock your elbows hard at the end.
Keep your shoulders down.
results.description: Push Pull Front Handle Push is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders.

results.name: Push Up and Rotation
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body. Perform a push-up.
As you push back up, shift your weight onto your left hand and rotate your torso to the right, raising your right arm towards the ceiling. Your body should form a T-shape.

Return your right hand to the floor and lower your body into another push-up. Repeat the movement, this time rotating to the left and raising your left arm towards the ceiling. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and rotate, and inhaling as you lower your body.
Ensure your body forms a straight line during the push-up and rotation, avoiding any sagging or arching of the back.
Keep your feet hip-width apart to provide a stable base for the rotation.
results.description: Push Up and Rotation is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back, Triceps.

results.name: Push Ups Bodyweight
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor, maintaining a straight body line and keeping your neck neutral.
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Lower yourself with control, ensuring your chest almost touches the floor while maintaining proper form.
Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
results.description: Push Ups Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Resistance Band Assisted Push-Up
instructions: Secure two loop elastic bands on a straight bar, ensuring they are securely anchored. Position each band over your shoulders.
Set yourself in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. The resistance bands should provide support as you perform the push-ups.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body. Allow the resistance bands to assist you as you descend.
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance bands are securely positioned over your shoulders and anchored to the straight bar to provide consistent assistance.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Lower yourself with control, ensuring your chest almost touches the floor while maintaining proper form.
Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
results.description: Resistance Band Assisted Push-Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chest Fly
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lean forward, extending your arms straight to the sides to form a T-shape. Your body should be in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly bring your hands together in front of your chest by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Return to the starting position by allowing your arms to extend back to the sides with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you bring your hands together and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your chest muscles to bring your hands together, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your core tight to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chest Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Core.
